body:
*Updated October 2026.*

Almost every RAG conversation we have starts with the same question: what will this cost? It is the right question, and it deserves a better answer than "it depends". Here is how RAG budgets actually break down in 2026, based on the systems we have built and shipped.

## The short answer

A production RAG system costs **$15,000–$30,000** to build. A pilot over a clean document set can land under $15,000; a complex deployment with messy formats, strict permissions, and serious evaluation requirements can push past $30,000. Monthly running costs are typically **$200–$2,000** depending on query volume and document scale.

## What drives the cost

### 1. Document ingestion complexity ($3,000–$10,000)

This is the biggest variable. Clean markdown and structured docs are cheap to ingest. Scanned PDFs, Office files with embedded tables, Confluence exports, and mixed-format archives are not — each format needs parsing, cleaning, and validation logic. A client with 50,000 clean help-center articles pays far less than one with 5,000 scanned legal PDFs.

### 2. Chunking and retrieval design ($2,000–$5,000)

Naive fixed-size chunking is free and usually wrong. Getting retrieval right means a chunking strategy matched to your document structure, embedding model selection, hybrid search (vector + keyword), and metadata filtering. This is where most DIY RAG projects fail — the demo works, production doesn't.

### 3. Permission-aware access ($2,000–$6,000)

If different users should see different documents, the retrieval layer must filter by access rights *before* generation. Retrofitting this later is painful; designing it in from the start is a modest line item. Skip it only if every user can see everything.

### 4. Evaluation harness ($3,000–$7,000)

A regression suite of real user questions, groundedness scoring, and quality tracking on every pipeline change. This is the difference between "it seemed fine in the demo" and "we know it works". Enterprise buyers should treat this as non-negotiable.

### 5. UI and integrations ($2,000–$5,000)

Chat widget, Slack/Teams integration, API access, or embedding in an existing product. A standalone chat interface is the cheapest; deep product integration costs more.

## Running costs

- **Vector database:** $0–$500/month (pgvector self-hosted is nearly free; Pinecone scales with usage)
- **Embedding + LLM API calls:** $100–$1,500/month depending on query volume
- **Maintenance:** expect 10–20% of build cost per year for model updates, re-indexing, and quality monitoring

## What a realistic budget looks like

| Scope | Build cost | Monthly run |
|---|---|---|
| Pilot, clean docs, one channel | $12,000–$18,000 | $200–$500 |
| Production, mixed formats, permissions | $20,000–$30,000 | $500–$1,200 |
| Enterprise, multi-source, strict evals | $30,000–$50,000 | $1,000–$2,000+ |

## How to keep costs down

1. **Start with your highest-value document collection**, not everything. Prove value, then expand.
2. **Clean your docs before we ingest them.** Every hour you spend on source quality saves three in pipeline work.
3. **Use managed vector databases early.** Self-hosting pgvector saves money at scale but costs engineering time you don't have yet.
4. **Don't skip evaluation to save money.** A RAG system nobody trusts costs infinitely more than one with a test suite.

## The bottom line

RAG is one of the highest-ROI AI investments a company can make — but only if it is built for production, not demoed into existence. The cost drivers above are the same ones that determine whether your system actually gets used.

If you want a fixed, scoped estimate for your documents, [book a free consultation](/services/rag-development) — we will look at your actual document set and give you a real number, not a range.
